rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation is at line 33 in instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine). InstanceNorm2dCustom defaults affine=True, creating defined weight/bias. The dispatch logic 'if (weight.defined() && bias.defined())' routes to instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine, which has unchanged shared_sq_sum[256]. The mutated kernel is never invoked.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies shared memory allocation in instance_norm_forward_kernel, the non-affine version of the kernel. However, ModelNew instantiates InstanceNorm2dCustom with the default affine=True parameter. This causes weight and bias to be defined nn.Parameter tensors. The CUDA dispatch logic then routes execution to instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine, which retains the original shared_sq_sum[256] allocation. The mutated kernel code path is architecturally unreachable regardless of input tensor values. No value-level test can trigger execution of the mutated code because kernel selection depends solely on whether weight/bias are defined, not on tensor values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed contract. Would require setting affine=False in InstanceNorm2dCustom constructor, which is a configuration change not permitted under the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing should consider model configuration coverage, not just input value coverage. When mutating kernel code with multiple dispatch paths (affine vs non-affine), ensure tests exercise all code paths by varying model configuration parameters like affine=True/False.
